title: Docs: Add FAQ about generic Vue components in CSF Next
body:
Related to #24238

Storybook maintainers cherry-pick bug and documentation fixes into the `main` branch as part of the release process, so you shouldn't need to worry about this. For additional guidance: https://storybook.js.org/docs/contribute

## What I did

Added a FAQ entry to the CSF Next documentation explaining how generic Vue components work with CSF Next.

Generic Vue components (using `<script lang="ts" setup generic="T">`) had type inference issues with traditional CSF3 (the generic type `T` would default to `unknown`). With CSF Next, users can simply pass the type parameter directly:

```typescript
const meta = preview.meta({
  component: GenericList<{ id: number; name: string }>,
});
```

This documents the solution to issue #24238.

🌐 Web query:

`OpenCode CLI environment variables detection`

💡 Result:

OpenCode CLI “detects”/uses environment variables in two main ways:

1) **CLI/runtime feature flags (read directly from your shell env)**
- OpenCode reads a set of `OPENCODE_*` variables at startup to toggle behavior (config paths, autoupdate, pruning, Claude-code file loading, server auth, etc.). ([opencode.ai](https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/?utm_source=openai))  
- Notable examples include `OPENCODE_CONFIG` (custom config file path) and `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` (inline JSON config), plus various feature toggles like `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE`, `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE`, etc. ([opencode.ai](https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/?utm_source=openai))

2) **Config discovery + env-var substitution (env vars referenced from config files)**
- **Config discovery precedence** (highest → lowest):  
  `OPENCODE_CONFIG` → `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` → `opencode.jsonc/json` in project dir → parent dirs → global config (typically under `~/.config/opencode/`). ([deepwiki.com](https://deepwiki.com/sst/opencode/7.1-cli-commands-reference?utm_source=openai))  
- Inside config files, OpenCode supports **env var interpolation** with `{env:VARIABLE_NAME}`; if the env var is missing, it substitutes an empty string. ([opencode.ai](https://opencode.ai/docs/config?utm_source=openai))

comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**`stdoutIsTTY` type should allow `undefined` to match `process.stdout.isTTY`.**

`process.stdout.isTTY` is `boolean | undefined`, but `DetectAgentOptions.stdoutIsTTY` is typed as `boolean`. When `isTTY` is `undefined` (e.g., piped output), the current logic at line 78 treats it as falsy and applies heuristics, which may cause false positives.

Consider:
1. Updating the type to `boolean | undefined`
2. Explicitly handling `undefined` in the logic (e.g., treat as non-TTY or skip heuristics)


<details>
<summary>🔧 Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
 type DetectAgentOptions = {
-  stdoutIsTTY: boolean;
+  stdoutIsTTY: boolean | undefined;
   env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;
 };
```

And optionally be explicit about undefined handling:
```diff
-  if (stdoutIsTTY) {
+  // When isTTY is true, skip heuristics (user is likely in an interactive terminal)
+  // When undefined or false, apply heuristics
+  if (stdoutIsTTY === true) {
     return undefined;
   }
```
</details>


Also applies to: 75-80

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In `@code/core/src/telemetry/detect-agent.ts` around lines 16 - 19, Update the
DetectAgentOptions type so stdoutIsTTY is typed as boolean | undefined (to match
process.stdout.isTTY) and modify the detection logic in the detect-agent routine
(the code that reads options.stdoutIsTTY and applies heuristics) to explicitly
handle undefined—either treat undefined as non-TTY (same behavior as false) or
bypass the heuristics path when stdoutIsTTY === undefined; ensure references to
DetectAgentOptions and any function using options.stdoutIsTTY are updated
accordingly so the undefined case no longer produces unintended false positives.
```

</details>
